parts.answer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.

questions.title: Car momentum–time graph — momentum, kinetic energy & acceleration

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Linear momentum is the product of the mass and the velocity of an object.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Maximum momentum read from Fig. 2.1 = 7.2×10⁴ N s
v = p/m = 7.2×10⁴ / 1800 = 40 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
a = (gradient of momentum–time graph)/m = Δp/(Δt×m)
= 3.6×10⁴ / (4.0 × 1800)
= 9.0×10³ / 1800 = 5.0 m s⁻² (at t = 4.0 s the momentum has risen linearly to 3.6×10⁴ N s)

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
The velocity rises linearly from 0 to 40 m s⁻¹ over 8.0 s, then falls linearly to zero over the next 4.0 s.
distance = area under the v–t graph = ½ × 40 × (8.0 + 4.0) = 240 m

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Sketch a stepped graph with no time delay at the step: a horizontal straight line at a = 5.0 m s⁻² from t = 0 to t = 8.0 s, a vertical step down at t = 8.0 s, then a horizontal straight line at a = −10 m s⁻² from t = 8.0 s to t = 12.0 s (the gradient of the p–t graph is constant at 7.2×10⁴/8 = 9.0×10³ N from 0 to 8 s, then −1.8×10⁴ N from 8 to 12 s).

questions.title: Motor lifting a load — work done, efficiency & coil current

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The work done by a force is the product of the force and the displacement moved in the direction of the force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
The block is raised at constant speed, so the lifting force equals the weight mg, where g is the acceleration of free fall (9.81 m s⁻²).
ΔEP = work done by the lifting force = force × distance = mg × Δh, so ΔEP = mgΔh.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
efficiency = useful output power / total input power
= 600 / 900 = 0.67

questions.title: Metal wires P and Q — Young modulus & spring constant

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The Young modulus is the ratio of (tensile) stress to (tensile) strain.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: A straight line of positive gradient passing through the origin (Hooke's law behaviour within the limit of proportionality).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The gradient represents the spring constant k = F/x of the wire.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The area under the line represents the elastic potential energy stored in the wire.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
x = FL/(AE). Wire Q has double the cross-sectional area and double the Young modulus of P, and — having the same volume as P but double its area — half the length of P.
x_Q/x_P = (L_Q/L_P) × (A_P/A_Q) × (E_P/E_Q) = ½ × ½ × ½ = ⅛
The extension of Q is ⅛ times the extension of P: extension is proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area and Young modulus.

questions.title: Beta decay of potassium-40 — decay equation & quark composition

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer:
Conserving nucleon number: 40 = P + 0, so P = 40; in β⁻ decay a neutron becomes a proton so the nucleon number is unchanged, Q = 40 − 20 = 20 → Q = 20.
Conserving charge: 19 = Q + S, so S = −1; the β⁻ carries no nucleons, so R = 0.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Particle Z is the (electron) antineutrino.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer: Both the β⁻ particle and the antineutrino belong to the class of fundamental particles called leptons.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
An alpha-particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons. A proton is made of up–up–down quarks and a neutron of up–down–down quarks, so:
2 protons + 2 neutrons give (2×2 + 2×1) up quarks and (2×1 + 2×2) down quarks
= 6 up quarks and 6 down quarks.

questions.title: Two coherent microwave sources — phase difference & interference

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: For maximum intensity, the waves from X and Y must arrive in phase at the point of detection. At O the two paths are equal, so the 90° phase difference between the sources is unchanged — the waves are not in phase at O, so O is not the position of greatest intensity.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a cross labelled B on line PQ, on the opposite side of O from A, with OB = OA — the intensity minimum closest to O is the same distance from O as the closest maximum A (both at path difference λ/4 = 0.003 m from O).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
At A the waves arrive in phase, so the path difference must cancel the 90° source phase difference: Δx = λ/4.
Δx = 0.012 / 4 = 0.0030 m

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
λ = ax/D → fringe spacing x = λD/a
x = (0.012 × 2.3) / 0.18
= 0.15 m

questions.title: Cell with internal resistance — terminal p.d., series & parallel resistors

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer:
Lost volts across the internal resistance = e.m.f. − terminal p.d. = 1.50 − 1.36 = 0.14 V
I = V/r = 0.14 / 0.28 = 0.50 A

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
combined resistance = terminal p.d. / current = 1.36 / 0.50
= 2.7 Ω

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer:
R = combined resistance − 1.0 = 2.72 − 1.0
= 1.7 Ω

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Complete Fig. 7.2 by connecting the two resistors (1.0 Ω and R) in parallel across the terminals of the cell, in series with the 0.28 Ω internal resistance, and no other components.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The external resistance is now smaller (the parallel combination of 1.0 Ω and 1.7 Ω is less than 1.0 Ω, whereas the series combination was 2.7 Ω), so a larger current flows and a larger fraction of the e.m.f. is dropped across the internal resistance. Hence the terminal p.d. is less than 1.36 V.
